summaryBox.title: Carbonyl Polarity & Approach Angle
summaryBox.takeaway: Planar sp² carbon with polarized Cδ+=Oδ-. Nucleophiles attack at the Bürgi-Dunitz angle (107°) to optimize HOMO-LUMO overlap with the π* orbital.

conceptBreakdown.content: The Carbonyl Group ($>\text{C=O}$) consists of an $sp^2$-hybridized carbon doubly bonded to oxygen ($1\sigma + 1\pi$ bond), displaying planar $120^\circ$ geometry. The $\text{C=O}$ bond is strongly polarized ($\overset{\delta+}{\text{C}}=\overset{\delta-}{\text{O}}$) due to oxygen's high electronegativity ($\chi = 3.5$ vs $2.5$). Nucleophiles approach at the **Bürgi-Dunitz angle of $107^\circ$** relative to the $\text{C=O}$ axis.

Reactivity Order: HCHO > RCHO > ArCHO > R-CO-R > Ar-CO-R > Ar-CO-Ar
conceptBreakdown.content:
- **Rosenmund Reduction**: $R\text{COCl} + \text{H}_2 \xrightarrow{\text{Pd/BaSO}_4, \text{ S/Quinoline}} R\text{CHO}$ (Formaldehyde cannot be made).
- **Stephen Reaction**: $R\text{-CN} + \text{SnCl}_2 + \text{HCl} \xrightarrow{\text{Ether}} R\text{-CH=NH}\cdot\text{HCl} \xrightarrow{\text{H}_3\text{O}^+} R\text{CHO}$.
- **DIBAL-H Reduction**: Selectively reduces nitriles and esters to aldehydes at $-78^\circ\text{C}$, leaving double bonds intact.
- **Etard Reaction**: $\text{Ph-CH}_3 + \text{CrO}_2\text{Cl}_2 \xrightarrow{\text{CS}_2} \text{Complex} \xrightarrow{\text{H}_3\text{O}^+} \text{PhCHO}$.
- **Gattermann-Koch**: $\text{Benzene} + \text{CO} + \text{HCl} \xrightarrow{\text{AlCl}_3/\text{CuCl}} \text{PhCHO}$.
- **Dialkylcadmium Route**: $2 R\text{COCl} + R'_2\text{Cd} \to 2 R\text{-CO-}R' + \text{CdCl}_2$ (does not react with ketones).

quickRevision: Bürgi-Dunitz angle is 107° for nucleophilic attack.
Reactivity: HCHO > RCHO > ArCHO > R-CO-R > Ar-CO-R > Ar-CO-Ar.
Rosenmund reduction uses poisoned Pd/BaSO₄ to stop at aldehyde.
DIBAL-H selectively reduces esters and nitriles to aldehydes at -78°C.
Dialkylcadmium (R'₂Cd) converts acid chlorides to ketones without over-addition.
